dataset.real_data: none: no public astronaut vital-sign time series is available without a data-use agreement

anomaly.selection: feature set per detector chosen by validation AUPRC; test used once for reporting

statistical.label: Statistical (personal baseline)
statistical.description: Largest robust z-score against the person's own time-of-day and activity baseline, with sustained deviation weighted up.

isolation_forest.label: Isolation Forest
isolation_forest.description: Ensemble of random trees; anomalies are isolated in fewer splits.

lof.label: Local Outlier Factor
lof.description: Density of each window relative to its 40 nearest normal neighbours.

autoencoder.label: Autoencoder
autoencoder.description: Neural network trained to reconstruct normal windows; large reconstruction error is anomalous.

ensemble.label: Ensemble (weighted mean of calibrated scores)
ensemble.member_rule: validation AUPRC >= 80% of the best; weight = AUPRC above base rate

limitations: All data is simulated by the ASTRA-MED simulator. Results show how well each method recovers the simulator's injected events and dynamics; they say nothing about accuracy on real astronauts.
The simulator's physiology, the injected events and the evaluation labels share one design, which makes the task easier than real monitoring, where events are unlabelled, heterogeneous and rare.
Planned activity equals actual activity in the simulator; real crew timelines deviate from plan.
Detection thresholds are calibrated on labelled validation data to a 1% window false-alarm rate. A real deployment would have no labels and would need clinician-reviewed calibration.
Prediction intervals are split-conformal; their coverage guarantee assumes exchangeability, which time series only approximate. Test coverage is measured and reported, not assumed.
No model here has been validated on astronaut or patient populations. Outputs are experimental decision support and must never be used as a diagnosis.
